title: Genetic Quantization-Aware Approximation for Non-Linear Operations in Transformers
problem: Non-linear functions in Transformers incur substantial and frequently underestimated hardware costs. Existing LUT-based approximation methods require high-precision FP/INT32 arithmetic and lack support for integer-only INT quantization.
motivation: Optimizing non-linear operations is critical for hardware-efficient Transformer deployment since their costs are frequently underestimated.
method: GQA-LUT uses a genetic algorithm to automatically determine parameters for piece-wise linear LUT approximation with quantization awareness. The algorithm enables INT8-based LUT implementation instead of high-precision FP/INT32. The approach is evaluated on semantic segmentation for both vanilla and linear Transformer variants.
key_novelty: Genetic algorithm framework with quantization awareness for automatic parameter optimization of LUT approximation, enabling efficient INT8 implementations.
contributions: Genetic algorithm-based framework (GQA-LUT) for automatic parameter determination in LUT approximation with quantization constraints
First approach enabling integer-only INT8 quantization for non-linear LUT approximation, previously requiring FP/INT32
81.3-81.7% area savings and 79.3-80.2% power reduction compared to high-precision alternatives with negligible accuracy loss on semantic segmentation
primary_theme: Genetic algorithm-based quantization-aware LUT approximation for efficient non-linear operations
